source.title: Anterior prefrontal cortex contributes to action selection through tracking of recent reward trends.

confidence_rationale: Lesion evidence that frontopolar cortex selectively supports crediting RECENT outcome trends to update the active contingency model (vs cumulative history) -- grounds the frontal contribution to crediting the currently-active rule/model for recent outcomes. Mixed/mid: it is contingency-model updating, not credit to a distinct rule object, and is correlational at the rule level.
failure_signatures: Frontopolar lesion abolished recent-trend extrapolation but left cumulative reward learning intact -- so a REE rule-field that credited only cumulative history (no recent-trend channel) would reproduce the lesion deficit, i.e. ARC-063 needs a recent-trend credit pathway distinct from cumulative accumulation.
The credited entity is a reward-contingency model, not an explicit rule; mapping to per-rule credit is an extension.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Patients with anterior-prefrontal (frontopolar) lesions showed a selective deficit in extrapolating the most recent reward trend (comparisons between the two most recent outcomes) while retaining intact cumulative reward learning; FPC is proposed to select and update models of reward contingency in dynamic environments.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-063 must credit the CURRENTLY-ACTIVE rule for RECENT outcomes (so a rule can be split/merged/retired on recent evidence), a channel distinct from slow cumulative statistics. FPC's selective role in recent-trend extrapolation grounds a frontal substrate for exactly that recency-weighted, model-updating credit the evidence-trace refinement loop needs.
mapping.mapping_caveat: FPC tracks recent reward TRENDS to update a contingency MODEL, not credit assigned to a labelled rule object. The mapping treats 'active contingency model' as the analog of 'active rule', which is reasonable but an extension; and the rule-level inference is correlational/lesion, not mechanistic.
mapping.source_context: Human anterior-prefrontal lesion patients (n=8) on a four-armed bandit, model-based analysis vs healthy controls.

confidence_components.notes: Good lesion study with model-based analysis. Mapping fidelity mid: contingency-model vs rule-object; lower transfer risk (human).
